cover_options.text: Mistral previews 1T-parameter model pitched for cyber defense; weights due in October
Mistral calls its new model the best US or European open-weight. Weights aren't out yet
Mistral pitches new AI for cyber defense; index ranks it behind top closed models

headline.text: An open-weight model with no weights yet

body.text: Mistral put Mistral Large 4 (nicknamed Le Chonk) in public preview via its API on Oct 6. Weights are due at the end of October. Until they ship, Artificial Analysis lists it as proprietary.

headline.text: 38 on the independent index. The leader has 58

body.text: Mistral Large 4 is up from 9 for Mistral Large 3 on the Artificial Analysis index, but Claude Opus 5.5 (Max) leads at 58. Mistral says its training run is ongoing and expects significant improvements.

headline.text: Best open-weight? Depends who is counting

body.text: Mistral says it is the best open-weights model from the US or Europe. Artificial Analysis calls it the most intelligent from outside the US and China, and ranks it below several Chinese open-weight models.

headline.text: Mistral's pitch: closed models can refuse or vanish

body.text: Mistral says closed-model filters block legitimate defensive work, attackers jailbreak those models anyway, and losing provider access mid-incident is a risk. It says ML4 can run in private clouds or on-premise.

headline.text: Closed US models have already hit limits

body.text: In June, the Trump administration temporarily limited distribution of OpenAI and Anthropic models over cyberattack concerns. Hugging Face earlier used Z.ai's GLM 5.2 in a breach after US models' guardrails blocked it.

headline.text: Ahead on one cyber test, behind on another

body.text: Artificial Analysis gives ML4 82% on CyberGym-E2E-AA, ahead of MiMo-V2.6-Pro (79%) and GPT-6 Luna (78%). On its Cyber Index, ML4 scores 50, behind MiMo-V2.6-Pro (56).

headline.text: Mistral says rivals score near zero by refusing

body.text: Mistral says Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on the vulnerability test because they refuse it. The-decoder.com notes the test measures provider policy as much as model capability.

headline.text: The part Mistral hasn't explained

body.text: Mistral says security firms, vetted partners and government agencies are red-teaming a version with reduced moderation. It does not explain how the model tells legitimate vulnerability research from attack prep.

draft.follow: Follow Helios Group to see whether the weights and license terms land at the end of October.

caption.text:
French AI lab Mistral put Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, into public preview on Oct 6 and is pitching it for cyber defense.

The weights, the trained parameters that let others modify and self-host a model, are due at the end of October, so it is not open-weight yet. The license terms are unknown until then. Mistral says it is the best open-weights model from the US or Europe. On the independent Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index it scores 38, well behind the leader, Claude Opus 5.5 (Max), at 58.

Mistral's argument is that closed models can block legitimate defensive work or be withdrawn mid-incident. It says Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra score near zero on a vulnerability test because they refuse the task. That claim comes only from Mistral, and the-decoder.com notes the test measures provider policy as much as model capability.

Would you rather run your own security model or use one from a closed provider?

Follow Helios Group to catch the end-of-October weights release and the license terms.

Source: the-decoder.com, Wired, TechCrunch, CNBC, Artificial Analysis (LinkedIn) and Mistral on X, all October 6, 2026.

edit_notes: Cover leads with Mistral (well_known true). 1T size is Mistral's figure (F3 claim_by Mistral); docs say 1.05T, so the number stays off body slides and only the cover uses '1T'.
Skipped quote slides: every quote is single-source, and the slides carry the same points through sourced facts.
Slide 4 shows the disagreement between Mistral's 'US or Europe' claim and Artificial Analysis's 'outside US and China' claim, rather than picking one.
Slide 6 is the single background slide (B2). It names the June restrictions and the Hugging Face case, sourced to Wired and CNBC, and does not claim they caused Mistral's pitch.
Split stat on slide 7 uses only independent Artificial Analysis numbers. Mistral's near-zero refusal claim is kept separate on slide 8 with attribution and the-decoder.com's caveat.
Left out the conflicting numbers: GPU count (3,800 vs 4,000), context window (1M vs 512k) and the Series D figures. Also left out pricing, because the launch discount is unclear.
Left out Mistral's company-reported 93.3% Lakera result and the coding scores, to keep the story on the cyber pitch and the gap to the frontier.
The caption glosses open-weight using the CNBC TERMS entry. It carries the license-unknown point (F14) because the slides had no room for it.
